land.text: the secularised Prince-Bishopric of Würzburg, held by the Electorate of Bavaria 1803-1805 (except about 826 km2 given to other princes), exchanged back for Tyrol at Pressburg

predecessors.note: Bavaria held the land from 1803 (Reichsdeputationshauptschluss) and gave it up at Pressburg; the Bavarian side is in kingdom-of-bavaria.

land.text: most of the grand duchy, which Bavaria made the Untermainkreis, now Lower Franconia (de page)

successors.note: Austrian-Bavarian treaty of 3 June 1814; the land went to Bavaria. Ferdinand returned to the Grand Duchy of Tuscany (grand-duchy-of-tuscany).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Electorate of Würzburg exists from 26 December 1805, a year before Cliopatria's first Würzburg shape. 'Daraufhin wurde Würzburg am 26. Dezember 1805 zum Kurfürstentum erhoben.' The land is the former Prince-Bishopric of Würzburg, given to Bavaria in 1803 (except about 826 km2 that went to other princes) and returned for Tyrol at Pressburg. The infobox gives no area.

ledger.note: 26 December 1805: Würzburg is made an electorate for Ferdinand of Tuscany. 'Daraufhin wurde Würzburg am 26. Dezember 1805 zum Kurfürstentum erhoben'; Bavaria gave up the principality in exchange for Tyrol in the Peace of Pressburg (26 December 1805, English page) and Ferdinand lost Salzburg to Austria. The infobox of the Ferdinand page dates his Würzburg rule 26 December 1805 to 3 June 1814. Cliopatria's first Würzburg shape is 1806 and is mislabelled.

region.text: the Prince-Bishopric of Würzburg: Würzburg, Schweinfurt's surroundings and Bad Kissingen; the Cliopatria 'Principality of Regensberg' 1806 shape carries it

ledger.note: 1806: the Electorate of Würzburg becomes the Grand Duchy. The English page: 'After the Holy Roman Empire was dissolved on 6 August 1806, the territory was elevated to the Grand Duchy of Würzburg' and on 30 September 1806 it joined the Confederation of the Rhine; the de page makes the title follow the accession ('Because Rhine Confederation members had to drop their Holy Roman Empire titles, he became Grand Duke'); the CoR table gives 23 September 1806. Month left out because the pages differ.

1810: Schweinfurt goes to the Grand Duchy of Würzburg. 'Assigned to the grand duke of Würzburg in 1810, it was granted to the Kingdom of Bavaria four years later'; the city had passed to Bavaria in 1802-1803. The English Würzburg page: 'the Grand Duchy acquired the territory of Schweinfurt' in 1810. The Cliopatria shapes carry it already from 1806.

region.text: Schweinfurt, the former free imperial city of Schweinfurt and its territory

ledger.note: 3 June 1814: Würzburg passes to Bavaria. 'Under an Austrian-Bavarian treaty of 3 June 1814, Ferdinand lost his possessions to the Kingdom of Bavaria'; Schweinfurt 'fell in 1814 to the Kingdom of Bavaria' (Schweinfurt page). The de page puts the end at the First Peace of Paris (30 May 1814) and 28 June 1814 for the transfer; the kingdom-of-bavaria dossier has the gain in June 1814.

region.text: the Prince-Bishopric of Würzburg: Würzburg, Schweinfurt's surroundings and Bad Kissingen; the Cliopatria 'Principality of Regensberg' 1806 shape carries it

ledger.note: 3 June 1814: the Grand Duchy of Würzburg is dissolved. Ferdinand was restored as Grand Duke of Tuscany (30 May 1814 in the Ferdinand page text; 27 April 1814 in its infobox) and the Congress of Vienna confirmed the end of Würzburg ('the Grand Duchy of Berg and the Duchy of Würzburg were abolished', CoR page). Most of the land went into Bavaria's Untermainkreis, now Lower Franconia (de page).

region.text: the Prince-Bishopric of Würzburg: Würzburg, Schweinfurt's surroundings and Bad Kissingen; the Cliopatria 'Principality of Regensberg' 1806 shape carries it

wars.name: War of the Third Coalition
wars.outcome: The Peace of Pressburg (26 December 1805) takes Salzburg from Ferdinand for Austria and gives him Würzburg, which Bavaria gave up in exchange for Tyrol.
wars.note: The page names the treaty, not the war; no ground in Würzburg was fought over.

wars.name: War of the Sixth Coalition
wars.outcome: On 26 October 1813, after Leipzig, 'Ferdinand dissolved his alliance with the First French Empire'; under the Austrian-Bavarian treaty of 3 June 1814 the grand duchy passed to Bavaria.
wars.note: The page does not describe any fighting in the grand duchy, so no zone.

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary; the state was the old Prince-Bishopric of Würzburg (minus about 826 km2 lost in 1803 and plus Schweinfurt in 1810), whose edge is drawn from the Cliopatria shape of the swapped row.

notes: All four Cliopatria shapes are marked wrong because the rows 'Grand Duchy of Würzburg' and 'Principality of Regensberg' are swapped (confirmed with the gazetteer: the Regensberg shapes contain Würzburg city cells, this row's contain none; the eu-20-g notes reach the same result). Corrections point at the Regensberg row by Cliopatria name; the principality-of-regensberg dossier points its corrections at this row. This row's 1806-1807 shapes are Dalberg's Aschaffenburg land and the 1811-1814 shapes the Grand Duchy of Frankfurt (grand-duchy-of-frankfurt has no Cliopatria row and no dossier in this group). The start is the electorate of 26 December 1805, a year before Cliopatria's first shape (new keyframe grand-duchy-of-wurzburg_1805); the kingdom-of-bavaria dossier has no matching loss of Würzburg in 1805-1806. The pages give no area, no 1 May 1806 possession date and no departments; the Salzburg-Bavaria exchange of 1810 and the Paris treaty of 28 February 1810 are not on the pages. The pages disagree on the end: 3 June 1814 (English page and Ferdinand infobox), 30 May and 28 June 1814 (German page); on the accession to the Confederation of the Rhine: 30 September 1806 (both Würzburg pages) and 23 September 1806 (CoR table). Ferdinand's Tuscan restoration is dated 27 April or 30 May 1814. The Würzburg client-state relation to France (CoR from 1806 to 26 October 1813) belongs to first-french-empire's vassal events. Place coordinates used because the gazetteer lacks the names: Schweinfurt (10.23E, 50.05N).
